title: Deciphering the mitophagy receptor network identifies a crucial role for OPTN (optineurin) in acute myeloid leukemia
model: MV4-11/MOLM AML, Cas9 + mt-mKeima; pairwise dual-guide screen of 14 mitophagy receptors (4,761 constructs)
contrast: Mitophagy-high vs -low sort after OA or DFP induction (3 vs 3), single-construct abundance
paper_calls: OPTN identified as the sole non-redundant mitophagy receptor (fewest genetic interactions); validated for AML proliferation and survival
barcs_calls: Single-gene abundance: PHB2 (FDR 4e-5) and FKBP8 required for mitophagy; OPTN not significant
named_hits: PHB2 strong (depleted in high); OPTN not recovered by single-gene abundance
verdict: BARCS's single-construct analysis identifies PHB2 and FKBP8 as the receptors whose knockout most reduces mitophagy, but it cannot address the paper's central OPTN claim, which rests on genetic-interaction scores between guide pairs that BARCS's single-gene model does not represent.
